name: Bluetooth LE scan and connect
plain: Scans for nearby BLE devices and connects to read or write their data.
meaning: Shows which gadgets, wearables, trackers and beacons are near the person. Scan results and device names can act as an indoor location or an identity of what the person owns.

android.permission: BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT (API 31); before that BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_ADMIN plus location
android.prompt_ui: Nearby devices prompt (Android 12+); location prompt before that
android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset if unused for months
android.store_policy: Play: no special declaration; neverForLocation flag lets a scan app skip the location link
android.note: Android 12 stopped requiring location for BLE scans if the manifest says neverForLocation.

ios.prompt_ui: Allow app to find and connect to Bluetooth accessories? (Allow / Don't Allow)
ios.note: Since iOS 13 the prompt is per app. Scan results for unknown apps are rate limited in the background and need explicit service UUID filters.

fields.name: device address
fields.range: random and rotating on both OS
fields.precision: iOS shows only a per-app UUID

limits.headline: Can find and connect to nearby Bluetooth gadgets once you allow Bluetooth
limits.user_action: You tap Connect to device or Scan for gadgets
can: Scan for nearby Bluetooth LE devices such as wearables, trackers and beacons
Connect to a device and exchange data with it
See device names, which can hint at what you own
Guess rough indoor position from nearby beacons
cannot: Scan before you answer the Bluetooth prompt
Scan freely in the background on iPhone; scans must name services and are rate limited
Learn your location from scans on Android 12 and later when the app declares it does not use them for location
limits.reach_label: Nearby gadgets, while you use it
limits.differs: iPhone shows one Bluetooth prompt per app; Android 12 and later shows Nearby devices, and older Android also needed location.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app scan for nearby Bluetooth LE gadgets and connect to read or send data.

marketing.name: Bluetooth Low Energy
marketing.pitch: Connect Android to low power devices like heart rate bands and sensors.

marketing.name: Core Bluetooth
marketing.pitch: Talk to low energy Bluetooth gadgets from your iPhone or iPad app.

story.for_you: The app asks to find nearby Bluetooth devices. If you say yes, it can connect to your heart band, lock or tracker. The phone shows a small dot or icon when it is scanning.
story.for_makers: This is the gateway for every smart gadget the maker sells. Without it, the hardware is useless. Scans can also show which gadgets and beacons are around, which is helpful for stores and risky for privacy.

use_cases.example: A heart rate strap streams your pulse live to a cycling app during a ride.
A medical device sends glucose readings to a diabetes app every few minutes.
A smart lock opens when you walk up and the app connects in the background.
A party game uses nearby phones as controllers or a toy robot connects over Bluetooth.
A store app picks up a beacon at the shoe aisle and shows a coupon.
A tracker finder app scans for lost keys.
A store counts how many phones walk by, which is a form of foot traffic measurement.

story.android_note: Android 12 no longer needs location for BLE scans if the app promises it will not use them to find you.
story.ios_note: On iOS the prompt is per app. Background scans must name the device type they look for and are rate limited.

technical_bounds: Background scans must filter by service UUID on iOS
Android 8+ throttles background scans (about 5 starts in 30 seconds)
Hardware MAC addresses are hidden from apps on iOS and randomized on Android

abuse: Scanning for nearby phones or tags to build a presence trail
